caption:
5 copy-paste prompts that turn ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini into a budgeting assistant: upload a bank statement or CSV and get a real income/expense table, spending categories, a savings plan, a debt payoff order, and a subscription cleanup.

Not financial advice — just a faster way to see your own numbers.

Save this before your next payday.

#budgeting #personalfinance #chatgpt #claude #aitools #moneytips #savingmoney

slides.title: prompts to build a real monthly budget
slides.sub: Upload your statement, copy, paste, done.
slides.voiceover: Here are five prompts that turn ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini into a budgeting assistant.

slides.name: The Table Builder
slides.sub: Turn a messy bank statement into a clean income vs. expense table.
slides.prompt: I'm uploading my bank statement as a [CSV/PDF]. Build a clean table with columns Date, Description, Category, and Amount. Add a summary at the top: total income, total expenses, and net savings for the period.
slides.voiceover: One. Upload your statement and get a clean income and expense table.

slides.name: The Category Sorter
slides.sub: See exactly where your money actually goes.
slides.prompt: Using the transaction table above, group every expense into categories like Rent, Groceries, Transport, Subscriptions, and Eating Out. Show each category's total and its percentage of my total spending, ranked from highest to lowest.
slides.tip: Ask a follow-up like 'which category grew the most vs last month' if you have two statements.
slides.voiceover: Two. Group every transaction into categories, ranked by how much you spend.

slides.name: The Savings Planner
slides.sub: A month-by-month plan for a goal you actually pick.
slides.prompt: I want to save [AMOUNT] in [NUMBER] months for [GOAL]. Based on my income and expense totals above, suggest a realistic monthly savings target and which categories I could trim to hit it, without listing this as financial advice.
slides.voiceover: Three. Turn a savings goal into a month by month plan from your own numbers.

slides.name: The Debt Payoff Order
slides.sub: A clear order to pay off what you owe.
slides.prompt: Here are my debts: [LIST NAME, BALANCE, INTEREST RATE FOR EACH]. Suggest a payoff order using both the avalanche method (highest interest first) and the snowball method (smallest balance first), and explain the trade-off between the two for my situation. This is not financial advice.
slides.tip: Bring this to a licensed advisor before making big decisions — use it to understand your options, not as final advice.
slides.voiceover: Four. Compare two payoff orders for your debts, side by side.

slides.name: The Subscription Cleanup
slides.sub: Find every recurring charge hiding in your statement.
slides.prompt: Scan the transaction table above for recurring charges (same amount, roughly monthly). List each one with its name, amount, and how many months it appeared. Flag any I might have forgotten I'm paying for.

lines: Streaming app — 3 months in a row

slides.voiceover: Five. Find every recurring charge you forgot you were paying for.

slides.title: Get more out of this pack
items: Most banking apps let you download a statement as CSV — it works better than a screenshot.
Same five prompts, new statement — watch the categories change over time.
Use the numbers to decide, not the AI's opinion — it's a calculator, not an advisor.
slides.voiceover: Export a real CSV, run this every month, and keep it factual.
